answer_part:
The CONTROL device formulation employs m-MeO-PEACl at 2.0 mg/mL as a key additive in the perovskite precursor solution, alongside 15.0 mg/mL MACl, to passivate defects in the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅I₃ perovskite layer. However, the methoxy group in m-MeO-PEACl introduces steric hindrance that limits its ability to uniformly passivate undercoordinated Pb²⁺ ions at grain boundaries and surfaces. This results in persistent trap states that enhance non-radiative recombination, directly contributing to the observed Voc deficit (1.176 V) and FF limitation (79.2%) in the CONTROL device. The incomplete passivation also exacerbates ion migration under operational stress, reducing charge carrier lifetime and causing Jsc to plateau at 25.35 mA/cm² despite the favorable perovskite bandgap. While m-MeO-PEACl provides initial crystallization control, its hydrophobic methoxy moiety impedes optimal interfacial contact with the 4,4,4-NA SAM layer, further hindering hole extraction efficiency and FF stability.  

Replacing m-MeO-PEACl with PMACl at an identical concentration of 2.0 mg/mL addresses these limitations by leveraging the phenylmethyl group’s superior binding affinity to Pb²⁺ defects without steric constraints. PMACl forms a more homogeneous quasi-2D capping layer that effectively suppresses surface recombination, directly elevating Voc through reduced Shockley-Read-Hall losses. The enhanced passivation also minimizes halide vacancy migration, improving film homogeneity and enabling higher Jsc by reducing bulk recombination. Crucially, PMACl’s compatibility with the 4,4,4-NA SAM promotes seamless energy-level alignment at the perovskite/HTL interface, boosting charge extraction and FF. Although PMACl may slightly reduce crystallite size compared to m-MeO-PEACl, the trade-off is favorable as the improved defect passivation outweighs minor morphological changes, avoiding the recombination losses dominant in the CONTROL. Other formulation elements remain unchanged—MACl (15.0 mg/mL) for bulk crystallization, 4,4,4-NA SAM (0.5 mg/mL), and PDADI passivation (0.5 mg/mL)—as they function optimally in isolation but were previously undermined by subpar surface passivation.  

This optimized formulation elevates device metrics significantly: Voc increases to a range of 1.16–1.20 V, Jsc rises to 26.0–26.4 mA/cm², and FF improves to 80.4–82.4%, culminating in a PCE enhancement from the CONTROL’s 23.606% to a range of 24.3–26.1%. The gains stem directly from mitigated interfacial recombination and stabilized charge transport, resolving the CONTROL’s primary failure modes of voltage loss and extraction inefficiency. Implement the following composition adjustment: substitute m-MeO-PEACl (2.0 mg/mL) with PMACl (2.0 mg/mL) in the perovskite precursor solution, retaining all other concentrations and materials unchanged.
control_device_fabrication: The fabricated device resulted in a PCE of 23.606%, with VOC of 1.17607 V, JSC of 25.3513 mA/cm², and FF of 79.1751%. By dissolving Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85I3 at 1.65 mol/L as the primary ingredient, the perovskite precursor was effectively prepared. The hole transport layer (HTL) was fabricated using the SAM solution of 4,4,4-NA. The 4,4,4-NA concentration is 0.5 mg/mL. The perovskite precursor solution is prepared by mixing 15.0 mg/mL of MACl, and 2.0 mg/mL of m-MeO-PEACl additive in the solvent. Then, the prepared precursor solution was spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s onto the ITO substrate. 150 µL CB was dripped onto the center of film at 15 s before the end of spin-coating. Subsequently the substrate was covered under a petri dish on a hotplate and annealed at 110 for 15 in ambient air at 20 % relative humidity. A passivation layer of PDADI (0.5 mg/mL) was applied to the sample surface by spin-coating to enhance device performance. The passivation layer was applied via spin-coating at 5000 rpm for 30 s. During spin-coating, 70 µL of passivator was drop-casted onto the sample at 6 s. And followed by annealing at 100 ℃ for 5 min. In details, SAM solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 3000 rpm for 30 s, and annealed at 100 °C for 10 min.
target_device_fabrication: With this engineering, the resulting PSCs obtained a PCE of 25.2585%, a VOC of 1.18319 V, FF of 81.3931%, and JSC of 26.2281 mA/cm². The perovskite composition is Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85I3, and the initial stock perovskite solution is 1.65 mol/L. For the SAM solution, 4,4,4-NA (0.5 mg/mL) was added to the previous solution. We add MACl (15.0 mg/mL) and PMACl (2.0 mg/mL). For the perovskite deposition process, the perovskite films were deposited using a two-step spin-coating process at 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s. 150 µL CB was dripped onto the center of film at 15 s before the end of spin-coating. The resulting wet perovskite films were annealed at 110 °C for 15 min. The passivator PDADI (0.5 mg/mL) was introduced into the system to improve material properties. The passivation solution was spin-coated at 5000 rpm for 30 s onto the perovskite film. At a timing of 6 s, 70 µL of passivator was introduced into the spinning passivation layer. Post spin-coating, the passivation layer was annealed at 100 °C for 5 min. In details, SAM solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 3000 rpm for 30 s, and annealed at 100 °C for 10 min.
